title: What does Japan's stress check program require, and what mental health training should employers give?
seoTitle: Japan stress check and mental health
description: Japan's stress check under ISH Act article 66-10, its April 2028 extension to workplaces under 50 workers, and MHLW mental health training topics.
shortAnswer: Article 66-10 of Japan's Industrial Safety and Health Act requires employers to have a physician, public health nurse or other qualified person run an annual stress check for workers, with results going to the worker and a physician interview on request. Workplaces with 50 or more workers must do it now; MHLW states it becomes mandatory for smaller workplaces from April 1, 2028. MHLW's mental health guideline sets training content for workers, managers and health staff.
keyTakeaways: Ordinance article 52-9 requires a stress check at least once a year covering three areas: causes of psychological burden at work, the worker's symptoms, and support from colleagues.
Results go to the worker, not the employer; the employer may receive an individual result only with the worker's written or electronic consent, and must then keep it for five years.

Workplaces under 50 workers have had only an effort duty under article 4 of the Act's supplementary provisions; Act No. 33 of 2025 makes the check mandatory, and MHLW gives the start date as April 1, 2028.
From April 1, 2027, MHLW Ordinance No. 112 of 2026 requires group analysis of results to use methods that cannot identify individuals.
MHLW's Guideline for Maintaining and Promoting Workers' Mental Health lists 7 training topics for all workers, 11 for managers and 15 for in-house occupational health staff.
regulator: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), enforced by Labor Standards Inspection Offices under each Prefectural Labor Bureau
appliesTo: Employers with workplaces of 50 or more regular workers (mandatory now) and all other workplaces (mandatory from April 1, 2028)
Physicians, public health nurses and trained nurses, dentists, psychiatric social workers and certified psychologists who run stress checks
Line managers and supervisors, who are the audience for line care training
HR, occupational health and health and safety committee members

sections.heading: What does article 66-10 of the Industrial Safety and Health Act require?

blocks.text: Article 66-10 of the Industrial Safety and Health Act (労働安全衛生法, Act No. 57 of 1972) requires employers to have a physician, public health nurse or other person specified by MHLW ordinance carry out a test of the degree of psychological burden (心理的な負担の程度を把握するための検査), known as the stress check ([Industrial Safety and Health Act, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/347AC0000000057)). The article then sets out a sequence of duties.

items: The person who ran the check notifies each worker of their own result, and may not give it to the employer without the worker's prior consent (article 66-10(2)).

If a worker with high stress who meets the ordinance criteria asks for it, the employer must arrange a physician interview, and must not treat the worker disadvantageously for asking (article 66-10(3)).
The employer records the interview result, hears the physician's opinion, and takes measures such as a change of workplace, reduced hours or fewer night shifts where needed (article 66-10(4) to (6)).
The Minister publishes a guideline on those measures, and the State endeavors to train physicians and others on how psychological burden affects health (article 66-10(7) to (9)).

blocks.text: The stress check is a screening and prevention tool, not a training requirement in itself. Its value for a training team lies in the duties around it: who may run it, who may see results, and the education MHLW's mental health guideline expects alongside it. This page reflects the position as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Who runs the stress check, how often, and who sees the results?

blocks.text: The check is run at least once a year by a qualified person, and individual results stay with the worker unless they consent. The detail is in articles 52-9 to 52-21 of the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health ([Ordinance, e-Gov](https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/347M50002000032)).

blocks.caption: Key stress check rules in the Ordinance on Industrial Safety and Health, as at November 2026
head: Ordinance article
Rule
rows: Regular workers are checked once within each year on three areas: causes of psychological burden at work, the worker's resulting physical and mental symptoms, and support from other workers
The check may be run by a physician, a public health nurse, or a dentist, nurse, psychiatric social worker or certified psychologist who has completed training set by the Minister
Anyone with direct authority over the worker's dismissal, promotion or transfer must not handle the implementation work
Consent to share an individual result must be in writing or electronic; if the employer receives results, it must keep a record for five years
The employer must endeavor to have results aggregated and analyzed by group and to act on the findings
A requested physician interview must be held without delay; the interview record is kept for five years
Employers with 50 or more regular workers report results to the Labor Standards Inspection Office electronically once a year

blocks.text: Article 66-10 is not among the offenses listed in article 120 of the Act, so failing to run the check is not itself a fined offense. Inspectors can still issue guidance, and the annual report under article 52-21 makes non compliance visible for larger workplaces.

sections.heading: When do workplaces with fewer than 50 workers have to run stress checks?

blocks.text: MHLW states that stress checks become mandatory for workplaces with fewer than 50 workers on April 1, 2028 ([MHLW stress check page](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/bunya/roudoukijun/anzeneisei12/)). Until then, article 4 of the Act's supplementary provisions reads the duty in article 66-10(1) as "行うよう努めなければ" (must endeavor to carry out) for workplaces that are not required to appoint an industrial physician, which in practice means those under 50 workers.

The change comes from the Act on Partial Amendment of the Industrial Safety and Health Act and the Working Environment Measurement Act (Act No. 33 of 2025), promulgated in May 2025. MHLW's June 2026 leaflet for small employers confirms the April 1, 2028 start and points to a Small Workplace Stress Check Implementation Manual published in February 2026, which sets out a privacy protecting approach suited to workplaces without an in-house physician ([MHLW leaflet for workplaces under 50 workers](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/001679776.pdf)).

blocks.title: Planning point for multi site employers
blocks.text: The 50 worker threshold applies per workplace (事業場), not per company. A company with a large head office and several small branches may already run stress checks at head office but have no process at the branches. Those branches need one by April 1, 2028.

sections.heading: What changes for group analysis in April 2027?

blocks.text: From April 1, 2027, group analysis must be done in a way that cannot identify individuals. MHLW Ordinance No. 112 of 2026, promulgated June 30, 2026, adds the words "特定の個人を識別することができない方法で" to article 52-14(1). The implementation circular says this writes the existing interpretation into the rule rather than changing practice, and that analysis which can identify individuals does not satisfy the effort duty and is not acceptable for privacy reasons ([MHLW circular Kihatsu 0630 No. 2](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/001716818.pdf)).

MHLW's accompanying leaflet states that, as a rule, group analysis should not be done where the unit is under 10 people, with narrow exceptions such as averaging the total score of all 57 questionnaire items ([MHLW group analysis leaflet](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/001725894.pdf)). Managers who receive group results need to understand this limit, which belongs in line care training.

sections.heading: What training does MHLW's mental health guideline expect?

blocks.text: The Guideline for Maintaining and Promoting Workers' Mental Health (労働者の心の健康の保持増進のための指針, Public Notice No. 3 of March 31, 2006, revised by Public Notice No. 6 of November 30, 2015) is issued under article 70-2(1) of the Act ([MHLW mental health guideline](https://www.mhlw.go.jp/content/11300000/001671565.pdf)). It organizes workplace mental health into four kinds of care: self care, line care by managers, care by in-house occupational health staff, and care using external resources. Section 6(1) says employers are to endeavor to provide education and information suited to each role.

blocks.caption: Training topics in section 6(1) of MHLW's mental health guideline, by audience
head: Audience
Number of topics
Examples of topics listed in the guideline
rows: All workers, including managers (self care)
Company mental health policy; basic knowledge of stress; how to notice one's own stress; preventing and coping with stress; value of seeking help; internal and external contacts
Managers and supervisors (line care)

Significance of workplace mental health care; assessing and improving the work environment; listening to and advising workers; supporting return to work after mental health leave; working with occupational health staff; protecting personal and health information
In-house occupational health staff

All of the above plus education and training methods, building a mental health plan and structure, referral to external resources, and specialist training suited to each role such as industrial physician or health officer

blocks.text: The guideline also suggests developing in-house trainers, and says that the in-house mental health promotion officer should not be a person with authority over dismissal, promotion or transfer, mirroring the stress check rule in article 52-10(2). These are guideline expectations rather than penal requirements, but inspectors and occupational physicians use them as the reference point.

blocks.text: To set refresh intervals for the guideline based modules, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles). Because managers who handle consultations also need harassment response skills, align line care training with [Japan's power harassment prevention obligations](/regulations/japan-power-harassment-prevention-obligations) and build both into one [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the guideline's topics for each of the four kinds of care as concepts linked to roles, alongside the statutory stress check steps. That lets a training team show which line care topics a manager has covered, and see quickly what changes for small sites in 2028.

faqs.q: Can a company's HR department run the stress check itself?
faqs.a: HR can handle administrative tasks, but article 52-10(2) of the Ordinance bars anyone with direct authority over the tested worker's dismissal, promotion or transfer from implementation work. The check itself must be run by a physician, public health nurse or trained dentist, nurse, psychiatric social worker or certified psychologist.

faqs.q: Do workers have to take the stress check?
faqs.a: The Act places the duty on the employer to carry out the check, not on workers to take it. MHLW's mental health guideline says it is desirable for all workers to take the check unless there is a special reason, and employers must not treat workers disadvantageously in connection with requesting a physician interview.

faqs.q: Is mental health training mandatory in Japan?
faqs.a: The education provisions are in MHLW's mental health guideline, which says employers are to endeavor to provide role based education and information. That is an effort duty rather than a penal requirement. Harassment prevention is different: employers have separate mandatory duties under the power harassment rules, including making their policy known to workers.

faqs.q: What does the 2025 amendment mean for a company with only small offices?
faqs.a: Each office under 50 workers must run an annual stress check from April 1, 2028. Such workplaces usually lack an in-house physician, so MHLW's February 2026 small workplace manual and its regional occupational health centers are the practical starting points for arranging implementers and physician interviews.

factCheck.claim: Article 66-10(1) to (9) require a stress check by a physician, public health nurse or other ordinance person; results go to the worker and need consent before the employer receives them; physician interview on request with no disadvantageous treatment; record, opinion and measures; guideline; State training effort. Article 120 lists 66(1) to (3), 66-3, 66-6 and others but not 66-10. Supplementary provisions article 4 reads the duty as an effort duty for workplaces outside article 13(1) (no industrial physician requirement).

Ordinance 52-9 annual check on three areas; 52-10 implementers (physician, public health nurse, or trained dentist, nurse, psychiatric social worker, certified psychologist) and exclusion of persons with dismissal, promotion or transfer authority; 52-13 written or electronic consent, 5 year record; 52-14 group analysis effort duty; 52-16 interview without delay; 52-18 interview record 5 years; 52-21 annual electronic report for 50 or more workers.
MHLW states that from April 1, 2028 (令和10年4月1日) stress checks are mandatory for workplaces with fewer than 50 workers, following the amended Act promulgated in May 2025.
MHLW leaflet (June 2026) confirms the April 1, 2028 start and the Small Workplace Stress Check Implementation Manual published February 2026.

MHLW Ordinance No. 112 of 2026, promulgated June 30, 2026 and in force April 1, 2027, adds a non identifying method requirement to article 52-14(1); the change codifies existing interpretation; identifying analysis does not satisfy the duty.
Group analysis should in principle not be carried out for units under 10 people, with exceptions such as averaging the total of all 57 items.

Mental health guideline (Public Notice No. 3 of 2006, revised No. 6 of 2015) issued under Act article 70-2(1) sets four cares; section 6(1) lists 7 topics for workers, 11 for managers and 15 for occupational health staff; suggests developing in-house trainers; the mental health promotion officer should not have personnel authority; it is desirable for all workers to take the stress check.
